<thought>The carbon NMR shows only three aliphatic carbon signals: 37.50 ppm, 36.39 ppm, and 26.41 ppm. Methyl carbons typically appear upfield (≈10–30 ppm). The 26.41 ppm signal is consistent with a methyl carbon, while the other two are more downfield, indicating methylene or tertiary carbons. Therefore, the molecule contains a single methyl group.</thought>
<final_answer>1</final_answer>
